inputs.original_text: Phoenix city leaders voted Wednesday night to tighten restrictions on ICE and other law enforcement agencies using city property. Whatever justification they offer, this puts political agendas ahead of cooperation with those charged with enforcing the law. When local officials weaken the ability of federal authorities to do their jobs, public order and community safety are the ones at risk.
inputs.modified_text: Phoenix’s leaders are putting political posturing ahead of cooperation with the people responsible for enforcing the law. Whatever procedural language surrounds this vote, restricting ICE and other law enforcement agencies from using city property risks undermining public order. Families need safe communities and officials who respect the rule of law—not leaders who make enforcement harder.
